description.narrative:
Project Outcomes Improved access to and quality of finance for microentrepreneurs, especially women entrepreneurs: Limited access to financial services remains one of the key factors limiting individuals, especially lower-income earners or those operating MSMEs, to participate in economic activities in Indonesia. According to Findex, only 18.4% of adults borrowed from a financial institution or used a credit card. IFC estimates the MSME finance gap to be US$166 billion (17% of the countrys GDP), out of which US$74 billion represents the microenterprises financing gap. Furthermore, according to the Ministry of Cooperatives and Small and Medium Enterprises of Indonesia, out of 64 million microenterprises as of 2020 in Indonesia, 52.5% were fully/partly financially constrained. Based on this backdrop, the proceeds of this investment will be utilized to increase access to finance for rural women microentrepreneurs by helping the company grow its microfinance portfolio as well as mobilize further funding from other international lenders, who are not equipped to lend to the rural women segment otherwise, via the platform.
Contribution to Market Creation Inclusiveness: Women microentrepreneurs are an underserved segment in financial services and are critical for inclusive development. This project by demonstration will encourage a more focused approach toward this customer base and lead to replication by similar financial institutions.
Contribution to Market Creation Integration: By introducing a tailored securitization structure and mobilizing significant funding from international investors, IFC will support deepening the capital markets and strengthening the product offering.

The proposed investment is in a senior tranche of asset backed securities in a Special Purpose Vehicle (the SPV or the Borrower) to be set up for pooling loan receivables which are originated by a peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platform owned by PT Amartha Nusantara Raya (Amartha or ANR or the Company). It is comprised of i) an IFC A loan of up to US$25 million and ii) mobilization of up to US$150 million, to improve access to finance for microentrepreneurs, especially women entrepreneurs (the Project) with up to 100% of the loan proceeds to be used for on-lending to women borrowers.

IFC's investment is expected to be utilized throughout the country.
